newsitem.title: UK: UK spot natgas trade lacklustre, prices steady.
newsitem.headline: UK spot natgas trade lacklustre, prices steady.

text.p: The U.K. spot natural gas market was lightly traded on Tuesday and prices were steady with little to push the market in either direction, traders said.
A few prompt deals were seen a slightly weaker levels than Monday's deals, with day ahead gas traded twice at 9.55 pence a therm (p/th), entry paid.
Transco reported a system buy on the flexibility mechanism on Monday at 0.3342 pence per kilowatt hour.
Further out, activity concentrated on the quarters, with Q1 and Q2 1998 both traded several at the top end of Monday's range.
"There's no dramatic change, things are at a bit of a stand-off," said one trader.
Q1 traded at least three times at 17.20 p/th, and Q2 changed hands at 11.425 and 11.45 p/th.
The fourth quarter of this year traded unchanged at 13.45 p/th.
Activity was brisk on the futures market, with the IPE contract recording its second busiest day since its launch at the end of January.
A total of 635 lots changed hands, after a record volume of 960 lots was posted last Thursday.
Brokers said that some players who used to stick exclusively to the over-the-counter market are now warming to futures trading.
"I think people are finally accepting it as an alternative to the OTC market... and on some days it even leads the market," said one.
